title: The morphism $\gamma_d:\underline{\operatorname{Hilb}}^d_{C/k}\to\underline{\operatorname{Pic}}^d_{C/k}$, $D\mapsto\mathcal O(D)$

source.place: Tag 0BA0 (lemma-picard-pieces), clause (4) 'for d >= 0 there is a canonical morphism gamma_d: Hilb^d_{X/k} -> Pic^d_{X/k}', and its proof, second paragraph: 'There is a morphism gamma_d ... coming from the invertible sheaf O(D_univ) on Hilb^d_{X/k} x_k X (Remark 0B9J) by the Yoneda lemma'

proof.text: *The family $C_T\to T$.* Let $T$ be any $k$-scheme and $f_T:C_T=C\times_kT\to T$ the projection [def-pc-base-change]. Since $C$ is a smooth projective curve [def-pc-smooth-projective-curve], in particular a curve over $k$ smooth over $k$, the morphism $f_T$ is smooth of relative dimension $1$ by [lem-sc-curve-base-change-relative-dimension-one]. It is flat and locally of finite presentation, being smooth [lem-pc-smooth-flat]. It is proper: $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is projective, hence proper [lem-pc-projective-proper], and properness is stable under base change [lem-pc-proper-base-change](1). A proper morphism is quasi-compact and separated, hence quasi-separated [def-weil-proper-morphism], so $f_T$ is of finite presentation (locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated, [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]). We use this for $T=H_d$, $T=\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ and $T=\operatorname{Spec}K$.

source.place: Remark 0B9J (remark-universal-object-hilb-d): 'The universal closed object is a relatively effective divisor ... by Lemma 0B9D', whose hypothesis 'X -> S smooth of relative dimension 1' is checked here for X = C_T

proof.text: *Clause 1.* Let $\varphi:h_{H_d}\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hilb}^d_{C/k}$ be the representing isomorphism [def-pc-representable-functor] and $D_d:=\varphi_{H_d}(\mathrm{id}_{H_d})$. By the definition of the Hilbert functor [def-pc-hilb-functor], $D_d\subset C_{H_d}$ is a closed subscheme with $D_d\to H_d$ finite locally free of degree $d$ [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. By step 1, $C_{H_d}\to H_d$ is smooth of relative dimension $1$, so [lem-pc-cartier-criterion], implication (1)$\Rightarrow$(2), shows that $D_d$ is a relative effective Cartier divisor on $C_{H_d}/H_d$ [def-pc-relative-effective-cartier]: an effective Cartier divisor of $C_{H_d}$, flat over $H_d$. (For $d=0$, $D_d=\emptyset$, whose ideal is $\mathcal O_{C_{H_d}}$; the argument covers it.) Hence its ideal $\mathcal I_{D_d}$ is an effective Cartier ideal and $\mathcal O(D_d)=\mathcal I_{D_d}^\vee$ of [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle] is defined, and it is an invertible $\mathcal O_{C_{H_d}}$-module by [lem-pc-divisor-line-bundle-invertible].

source.place: Remark 0B9J: 'The universal closed object is a relatively effective divisor D_univ ... by Lemma 0B9D ... In particular, D_univ is an effective Cartier divisor and we obtain an invertible module O(D_univ)'; Lemma 0B9D (lemma-divisors-on-curves) (1)=>(2)

proof.text: *The fibre of $\mathcal O(D_d)$ at a point.* Let $t\in H_d$, with residue field $\kappa(t)$ (a field extension of $k$ through $H_d\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, [def-pc-field-extension]) and canonical morphism $\iota_t:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)\to H_d$. The fibre product $C_{H_d}\times_{H_d}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)=(C\times_kH_d)\times_{H_d}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ is $C_{\kappa(t)}=C\times_k\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ (pasting of fibre products, [def-pc-fibre-product]), and the pullback of $\mathcal O(D_d)$ along the projection $\iota_{t,C}:C_{\kappa(t)}\to C_{H_d}$ is the fibre $\mathcal O(D_d)_t$ of [def-pd-fibrewise-degree]. By step 1, $C_{H_d}\to H_d$ is flat of finite presentation, and by step 2 $D_d$ is a relative effective Cartier divisor on it; so [lem-pc-recd-pullback] with $g=\iota_t$ gives: $D_t:=D_d\times_{H_d}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ is a relative effective Cartier divisor on $C_{\kappa(t)}/\kappa(t)$, in particular an effective Cartier divisor on $C_{\kappa(t)}$ [def-pc-relative-effective-cartier], and $\mathcal O_{C_{\kappa(t)}}(D_t)\cong\iota_{t,C}^*\mathcal O(D_d)=\mathcal O(D_d)_t$. Moreover $D_t\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ is the fibre of $D_d\to H_d$ over $t$, so, $D_d\to H_d$ being finite locally free of degree $d$, $\dim_{\kappa(t)}\Gamma(D_t,\mathcal O_{D_t})=d$ by [def-pc-finite-locally-free].

source.place: Remark 0B9J, last sentence: 'the restriction of O(D_univ) to the fibre [D] x X is O_X(D)', here at an arbitrary point t of H_d

proof.text:
*Clause 2: the fibrewise degree is $d$.* The scheme $C_{\kappa(t)}$ is proper over $\kappa(t)$ (step 1) and of dimension $1$ by [lem-pc-dim-base-change] ($C$ is a curve over $k$, $\kappa(t)/k$ a field extension). $D_t$ is an effective Cartier divisor on it (step 3), so [lem-pc-degree-base-change](2) gives $\deg\mathcal O_{C_{\kappa(t)}}(D_t)=\dim_{\kappa(t)}\Gamma(D_t,\mathcal O_{D_t})=d$, with $\deg=\chi(-)-\chi(\mathcal O)$ of [def-pc-degree-line-bundle]. Isomorphic invertible modules have the same Euler characteristic, so by step 3 and [def-pd-fibrewise-degree]
$$\deg_{H_d}(\mathcal O(D_d))(t)=\deg_{C_{\kappa(t)}}(\mathcal O(D_d)_t)=\deg\mathcal O_{C_{\kappa(t)}}(D_t)=d$$
for every $t\in H_d$.

source.place: Tag 0BA0 proof, first paragraph: Pic^d consists of the L with chi(X_t, L_t) = d + 1 - g, i.e. fibre degree d; the degree of O(D) for D of degree d

proof.text: *Definition of $\gamma_d$.* The isomorphism class $[\mathcal O(D_d)]\in\operatorname{Pic}(C_{H_d})$ is an element of the Picard presheaf at $H_d$ [def-pc-picard-presheaf]; let $c\in\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}(H_d)$ be its image under the sheafification map [def-pc-picard-functor]. The degree of $c$ [def-pd-degree-morphism], computed with the trivial covering $\{\mathrm{id}_{H_d}\}$ and the representative $\mathcal O(D_d)$, is the function $t\mapsto\deg_{H_d}(\mathcal O(D_d))(t)$, identically $d$ by step 4; so $c\in\operatorname{Pic}^d_{C/k}(H_d)$. With $\psi:\operatorname{Pic}^d_{C/k}\xrightarrow{\sim}h_{P_d}$ the representing isomorphism [def-pc-representable-functor], put $\gamma_d:=\psi_{H_d}(c)\in\operatorname{Hom}_k(H_d,P_d)$. This is the morphism of clause 2; equivalently, by the Yoneda lemma [lem-pc-yoneda], $\gamma_d$ is the morphism $h_{H_d}\to h_{P_d}$ given by $\psi\circ\tau\circ\varphi^{-1}$, where $\tau:h_{H_d}\to\operatorname{Pic}^d_{C/k}$ is the transformation corresponding to $c$.

source.place: Tag 0BA0 proof, second paragraph: 'There is a morphism gamma_d ... coming from the invertible sheaf O(D_univ) on Hilb^d x_k X (Remark 0B9J) by the Yoneda lemma (Categories, Lemma 001P)'

proof.text:
*The $K$-point $x$ and its divisor.* Let $K/k$ be a field extension and $x:\operatorname{Spec}K\to H_d$ a $k$-morphism. By the Yoneda lemma [lem-pc-yoneda], the natural isomorphism $\varphi$ is determined by $D_d=\varphi_{H_d}(\mathrm{id})$: $\varphi_{\operatorname{Spec}K}(x)=\varphi_{\operatorname{Spec}K}(\mathrm{id}_{H_d}\circ x)=\operatorname{Hilb}^d_{C/k}(x)(D_d)$, and the action of the Hilbert functor [def-pc-hilb-functor] on the morphism $x$ is base change, so this is $D:=D_d\times_{H_d}\operatorname{Spec}K\subset C_K$; being an element of $\operatorname{Hilb}^d_{C/k}(\operatorname{Spec}K)$, it is a closed subscheme finite locally free of degree $d$ over $K$. Applying [lem-pc-recd-pullback] as in step 3 with $g=x$ (allowed by steps 1 and 2): $D$ is a relative effective Cartier divisor on $C_K/K$, hence an effective Cartier divisor on $C_K$ [def-pc-relative-effective-cartier], and
$$\mathcal O_{C_K}(D)\cong x_C^*\mathcal O(D_d),$$
where $x_C:C_K\to C_{H_d}$ is the base change of $x$ and $x_C^*$ the pullback of modules [def-pc-module-pullback].

source.place: Remark 0B9J, last sentence (restriction of O(D_univ) to the fibre over the point [D] is O(D)), for a K-point; Proposition 0B9I (2) 'Part (2) follows from the definitions'

proof.text: *Clause 3.* By naturality of $\psi$ applied to $x$: $\gamma_d\circ x=h_{P_d}(x)(\gamma_d)=h_{P_d}(x)(\psi_{H_d}(c))=\psi_{\operatorname{Spec}K}\bigl(\operatorname{Pic}^d_{C/k}(x)(c)\bigr)$. The restriction map of the Picard presheaf along $x$ is pullback along $x_C$ [def-pc-picard-presheaf, def-pc-module-pullback] and the sheafification map is natural [def-pc-picard-functor], so $\operatorname{Pic}^d_{C/k}(x)(c)$ is the image in $\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}(\operatorname{Spec}K)$ of $[x_C^*\mathcal O(D_d)]=[\mathcal O_{C_K}(D)]$ (step 6). Hence the $K$-point $\gamma_d\circ x$ of $P_d$ corresponds under $\psi$ to the class of $\mathcal O_{C_K}(D)$ in $\operatorname{Pic}^d_{C/k}(\operatorname{Spec}K)$, where $D$ is the divisor corresponding to $x$.

Statement unchanged; stmt_deps gained def-pc-relative-effective-cartier, def-pc-finite-locally-free, def-pc-base-change, def-sc-effective-cartier-divisor, which the statement uses. lem-pc-universal-divisor (Lean-closed) was not cited: its node statement covers only degree d+1 >= 1, the scheme underline Hilb, and k-rational points, while the item needs every d >= 0, any representing H_d, and K-points; its Lean declaration isRelativeEffectiveCartier_universal_hilbertPresheaf does cover clauses 1 and the pullback part of step 6 in full generality. lean.statement: theorem exists_hilbertToPicardMorphism {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsSepClosed k] {C : Scheme.{u}} (f : C ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [f.IsSmoothProjectiveCurve] [GeometricallyIntegral f] (d : ℕ) (H P : Over (Spec (.of k))) (eH : (hilbertPresheaf f d).RepresentableBy H) (eP : (picardFunctorDegree f d).obj.RepresentableBy P) : let D := (eH.homEquiv (𝟙 H)).1 D.IsRelativeEffectiveCartier (pullback.snd f H.hom) ∧ D.toModulesᵛ.IsInvertible ∧ ∃ L : (pullback f H.hom).Pic, Nonempty ((fromSkeleton _).obj L.val ≅ D.toModulesᵛ) ∧ (∀ t : H.left, picardPresheafDegree f L t = (d : ℤ)) ∧ ∃ (hL : L ∈ (picardSubfunctorDegree f d).obj (op H)) (γ : H ⟶ P), eP.homEquiv γ = (toSheafify (Scheme.fppfTopology.over (Spec (.of k))) (picardSubfunctorDegree f d).toFunctor).app (op H) ⟨L, hL⟩ ∧ ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (x : Over.mk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))) ⟶ H), let T := Over.mk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))) let DK := (eH.homEquiv x).1 DK.IsInvertible ∧ DK.toModulesᵛ.IsInvertible ∧ ∃ (LK : (pullback f T.hom).Pic) (hLK : LK ∈ (picardSubfunctorDegree f d).obj (op T)), Nonempty ((fromSkeleton _).obj LK.val ≅ DK.toModulesᵛ) ∧ eP.homEquiv (x ≫ γ) = (toSheafify (Scheme.fppfTopology.over (Spec (.of k))) (picardSubfunctorDegree f d).toFunctor).app (op T) ⟨LK, hLK⟩
